## Solution

A regular icosahedron has **20 triangular faces**. We assign the distinct labels 1, 2, …, 20 to these faces, one label per face. Two assignments are considered the same if one can be rotated into the other, so we count labelings up to the action of the **rotation group** of the icosahedron.

### Step 1: Order of the rotation group

The rotation group of a regular icosahedron (equivalently, the regular dodecahedron, its dual) is the icosahedral group $A_5$, of order

$$|G| = 60.$$

(One way to see this: the icosahedron has 20 faces, each an equilateral triangle; a face can be sent to any of the 20 faces, and once the image face is chosen, the triangle can be rotated into 3 positions, giving $20 \times 3 = 60$ rotations.)

### Step 2: Burnside's lemma

By Burnside's lemma, the number of distinct labelings is

$$N = \frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g \in G} |\operatorname{Fix}(g)|.$$

Consider any non-identity rotation $g \neq e$. The action of $g$ on the 20 faces is a non-trivial permutation. A labeling (a bijection from faces to $\{1,\dots,20\}$) is fixed by $g$ only if the labeling is constant on every cycle of $g$'s permutation of the faces. Since all labels are **distinct**, this is possible only if every cycle has length 1, i.e. only if $g$ acts as the identity. But $g \neq e$, so $g$ has at least one cycle of length $\geq 2$, forcing at least two faces in the same cycle to receive the same label — impossible with distinct labels.

Therefore

$$|\operatorname{Fix}(g)| = 0 \quad\text{for all } g \neq e, \qquad |\operatorname{Fix}(e)| = 20!.$$

### Step 3: Compute

$$N = \frac{1}{60}\bigl(20! + 0 + \cdots + 0\bigr) = \frac{20!}{60}.$$

Now $20! = 2\,432\,902\,008\,176\,640\,000$, so

$$N = \frac{2\,432\,902\,008\,176\,640\,000}{60} = 40\,548\,366\,802\,944\,000.$$

### Verification

$40\,548\,366\,802\,944\,000 \times 60 = 2\,432\,902\,008\,176\,640\,000 = 20!$. ✓

### Answer

The number of distinct ways to assign the numbers 1 through 20 to the faces of a regular icosahedron, up to rotation, is

$$\boxed{40\,548\,366\,802\,944\,000}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
